question: Adelaar & Schapper (2024), the historical chapters 2, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13 and 36 (gap audit of 26 November 2026): what is entered from their tables?
chosen_reading: Three rows: Long Terawan Berawan *bʰ > pp, *dʰ > t͡ʃ, *jʰ > t͡ʃ (Smith 2024, Table 8.1). The other tables summarise works whose rows are already in (PAn > PMP mergers; Smith 2017a; Mead 2003; Mills 1975; Adelaar 1994a; Grimes & Edwards 2026), are wordlists (Tables 10.1-10.3, 9.4), or need a lect or node that does not exist.
alternatives: Add Proto-Philippines with the phoneme system of Table 7.1 (Blust p.c. in Zorc et al. 2024: 88); decision blust1991-pph is open. Enter Adelaar's (1992) Proto-Malayic inventory from Tables 9.1-9.2 (Anderbeck 2024: 112-113) as the sourced inventory of Proto-Malayic; decision adelaar1992-pm is open. Add Proto-Sangiric (Table 12.1, twelve etyma after Sneddon 1984), the Butonic languages Kaisabu, Cia-Cia, Kumbewaha and Lasalimu (Table 12.3, PMP *q) and Rampi (Table 12.9). Enter the consonant inventories of Buru and South Nuaulu from Table 36.1 (Grimes 2024: 599, after C. Grimes 1991 and Bolton 1990; consonants only, no vowel table) and add Asilulu. Give 'Lun Dayeh' of Table 8.1 (f, s, s) to one of the two Lun Dayeh dialects. Table 13.7 (Zobel 2024: 178; *z, *d, *j, *R in 21 CMP languages) was compared with the composed rows from Grimes & Edwards (2026) for Bima, Havu, Proto-Central Flores, Proto-Flores-Lembata and Buru only; the other 16 could be compared cell by cell.
